To find the indefinite integral of the function \(-\frac{14x}{3 \sqrt[3]{7-7x^2}^2}\), we first simplify the integrand. The expression \(\sqrt[3]{7-7x^2}^2\) is equivalent to \((7-7x^2)^{2/3}\), so the integrand can be rewritten as \(-\frac{14x}{3(7-7x^2)^{2/3}}\). 

We use the substitution \(u = 7 - 7x^2\). Differentiating this gives \(du = -14x \, dx\), which means \(-14x \, dx = du\). Substituting into the integral, we get:
\[
\int -\frac{14x}{3(7-7x^2)^{2/3}} \, dx = \frac{1}{3} \int u^{-2/3} \, du.
\]
Integrating \(u^{-2/3}\) with respect to \(u\) gives \(3u^{1/3}\), since the antiderivative of \(u^n\) is \(\frac{u^{n+1}}{n+1}\) for \(n \neq -1\). Thus, the integral becomes:
\[
\frac{1}{3} \cdot 3u^{1/3} + C = u^{1/3} + C.
\]
Substituting back \(u = 7 - 7x^2\), we obtain the final result:
\[
\sqrt[3]{7 - 7x^2} + C.
\]
